_doc: Wartime force posture the equipment counts don't show. drone_saturation (0..1): how densely a country's front is watched and struck by small drones (1 = millions a year, the 2025 Ukrainian front's 'kill zone'). An attacker advancing into such a front slows by up to DRONE_ADVANCE_DRAG (conflict/land_warfare.py). mobilised: already on a war footing at the start date, so no further wartime expansion beyond replacing losses. hosts: belligerents this country lets attack from its territory without itself joining the war, for hosting_days after the war starts. active_share: share of a GFP land-equipment count that is with units rather than in long-term storage (GFP counts both; stored equipment fights only once refurbished). Countries not listed: no drone saturation, not mobilised, host no one. reach_per_hop: supply reach per 150 km beyond consolidated ground, for armies whose logistics are not rail-bound (default 0.6).

UKR.basis: A few Bayraktar TB2s and commercial quadcopters; ~250,000 active troops before the invasion (Zelensky, May 2022). Equipment: ~987 battle-ready tanks (IISS Military Balance, as cited by the Modern War Institute) against GFP's 2,596 (active share 0.38, applied to all land equipment; low confidence).

RUS.basis: Orlan-10 reconnaissance drones for artillery spotting; no mass strike drones (140,000 drones delivered in 2023, per Putin, from a far smaller base). Equipment: IISS Military Balance 2022 counts 3,417 battle-ready tanks (army 2,927, naval infantry 330, airborne 160) and ~10,200 in storage; GFP's 12,420 counts both (active share 0.275, applied to all land equipment).

BLR.basis: ~30,000 Russian troops in Belarus for the 'Allied Resolve' exercise in February 2022; the offensive on Kyiv was launched from Belarusian territory (UN General Assembly resolution ES-11/1, 2 March 2022, deplored Belarus's involvement). The arrangement covered that opening offensive: Russian forces left the Belarus-launched axes by 6 April 2022 and did not attack from Belarus again.

USA.basis: Truck- and air-borne logistics: in 2003 the 3rd Infantry Division drove ~300-350 miles from Kuwait to Baghdad in 14-17 days of combat, supplied by convoys (about 200 tanker loads of fuel a day) though with stretched supply lines. Rail-bound armies keep the default 0.6 per 150 km (Russia: Vershinin, 'Feeding the Bear', War on the Rocks, Nov 2021). At 0.85, ~500 km of advance leaves ~57% of strength, against ~18% for a rail-bound army.

UKR.basis: More than 1.3 million drones delivered to the armed forces in 2024, production above 2.5 million a year (Kyiv Post); drones score ~85% of battlefield hits (Zelensky, 2025). General mobilisation since 24 February 2022: ~900,000 active.

RUS.basis: Production raised tenfold to ~1.4 million drones in 2024 (Putin, September 2024). Partial mobilisation (September 2022) and contract recruitment: ~1.32 million active. Equipment: ~1,750 tanks with units and ~4,000 in storage, much of it unrecoverable (IISS Military Balance 2025, as reported); GFP's 5,630 counts both (active share 0.31).
